title: The application serves a public status page listing every declared component and its current state
description: The application serves a public status page at a stable HTTP path intended for external readers (users, partners, unauthenticated visitors). The page renders a list of declared components (subsystems the project chooses to publish state for), each with a current state field from a fixed enum (operational, degraded, outage, maintenance) and a human-readable component name. The page has no login gate. The component list, the enum, and the display order are declared at boot from application configuration; no component appears on the page that was not declared.
rationale: External readers need a single canonical answer to 'is the service up right now' without support tickets. A public status page bounded by a declared component list is the industry-standard shape; the declared-list constraint is what stops the page from silently gaining or losing surfaces across deploys.
